note: Attacker-controlled raw input bytes are parsed as a tar archive or treated as a raw font file; the first file becomes the font data passed to FT_New_Memory_Face.
The font face is created from the attacker-controlled font bytes, which triggers parsing of the sfnt tables including CPAL and COLR.
The CPAL table header is parsed; num_colors is read from the font data and used later to bound color array accesses, but the vulnerable code path does not validate color indices against it.
The colors array pointer is set to the offset within the CPAL table; the array contains num_colors RGBA entries (4 bytes each).
The color_indices array pointer is set to the palette index array; each palette has a 2-byte index into the colors array.
The number of palette entries is read from the CPAL header; this value determines how many color records are read in tt_face_palette_set.
A heap buffer of num_palette_entries FT_Color records is allocated for the default palette.
The default palette (index 0) is loaded immediately during CPAL table parsing, invoking the vulnerable tt_face_palette_set function.
The offset into color_indices is computed for palette_index=0; this points to the first 2-byte color index in the CPAL table.
A 16-bit color index is read from the font data via FT_PEEK_USHORT(offset). This index is used to compute the starting pointer into the colors array without any bounds check against cpal->num_colors.

code: q->blue = FT_NEXT_BYTE(p); q->green = FT_NEXT_BYTE(p); q->red = FT_NEXT_BYTE(p); q->alpha = FT_NEXT_BYTE(p);
note: The loop reads num_palette_entries * 4 bytes starting from p. If color_index + num_palette_entries > num_colors, the reads extend past the end of the heap-allocated colors buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ of 1 byte.

code: limit = q + face->palette_data.num_palette_entries; while (q < limit) { ... q++; }
note: The loop iterates num_palette_entries times, each time reading 4 bytes (blue, green, red, alpha) from the colors array. With a crafted color_index value near 0xFFFF and a non-zero num_palette_entries, the reads go far beyond the allocated colors buffer, triggering the ASAN heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
